finding: WRITTEN AUTHOR CANDIDATE, UNREVIEWED. The extra-triangle bridge admits a universal strengthening: every order-10 1-RQLS whose cell rays all lie in a 3D subspace H or H-perpendicular has at most 95 distinct rays, for ANY resolution Latin square. No Z2 quotient, flatness, covariance, support coordinates or selected examples are assumed. Consequently a maximal witness cannot have an orthogonal 3+7 sector split.
argument: The 30 H-cells form 30 context triples. If K=30-D is their number of distinct rays and F the number of distinct ray-bases, repeated context triples obey 30-F<=binom(D,2): two different ray-bases share at most one ray in C3, and each occurrence of a repeated ray triple uses a distinct pair of its cells. The graph of K rays and contextual orthogonality is C4-free, with degrees 2t_i and sum t_i=3F; therefore sum binom(2t_i,2)<=binom(K,2). For D=0,1,2,3,4 the lower bounds on that sum are respectively 450,474,459,405,336, exceeding 435,406,378,351,325. Hence D>=5 and total cardinality<=70+25=95.
exact_checks: Exact integer kernel computed all five table entries and checked the elementary multiplicity inequality for 27000 integer triples. These finite checks supplement, not replace, the all-integer written proof.
